content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate candy with dried fruit are small sweets coated in milk or dark chocolate and filled with pieces of dried fruits such as raisins, apricots, cherries or figs. The combination of sweet chocolate and slightly tart, aromatic dried fruit makes them a popular snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dried fruits in the candies retain most of the vitamins and minerals they contain when fresh.
These candies first appeared in Europe in the 19th century as a way to make dried fruit more appealing to children.
The chocolate used often contains a small amount of emulsifiers to give a smooth texture.
The chocolate‑fruit combo improves iron absorption from the fruit thanks to the vitamin C present in some varieties.
In several countries the candies are considered a traditional holiday gift.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Dark chocolate is rich in flavonoids that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dried fruits provide dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Dried fruits supply potassium, magnesium and iron, important for heart and muscle function.

items.title: Quick energy boost
items.content: Sugars from chocolate and dried fruit rapidly replenish blood glucose levels.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Chocolate stimulates the production of serotonin and endorphins, which can lift mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption can contribute to weight gain and raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Allergy to cocoa or nuts
items.content: Some versions contain nuts or milk chocolate, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Acidity of dried fruits
items.content: Large amounts may irritate the stomach in people with high acidity.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: A typical serving (30 g) provides about 150–180 kcal, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the candies as a stand‑alone snack, stir them into yogurt or muesli, or use them as a sweet filling in baked goods. Slightly warming them makes the chocolate softer.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the candies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer storage, refrigerate to prevent the chocolate from melting.
